title: Not all trackers are that bad
body:
To give an example. Some trackers are aimed at improving user experience and do care about privacy. But I noticed that even these trackers are counted as being bad?
For example Countly, the tracker we use and run on premise just to protect our users their privacy while still being able to improve the app.

A lot of trackers/analytics/saas startups (I myself know at least 3) are aiming to allow some kind of analytics without impacting the privacy of the user. They should be rewarded for their efforts.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Exodus never say if a tracker is "bad" or even "good", trackers listed in exodus are added according to the following definition :
```
A tracker is a piece of software meant to collect data about you or your usages.
```
If a tracker is "good", it's in fact always a tracker.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: Ok, but why are they shown as orange/red? Because that clearly states they are bad. Maybe there should be a 4th color when only trackers are used that are privacy centric. (So obviously not for trackers like Google Analytics, Flurry, FB, etc.) But for trackers that do not leak any tracking info to 3rd parties.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
@Bramzor The trackers individually are not shown as orange/red, the color is only here to give a quick view on the number of trackers (see https://exodus-privacy.eu.org/en/page/faq/).

We cannot (**and don't want to**) identify whether a tracker is "privacy centric", bad or good, as @codeurimpulsif said :).

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
May I suggest changing the color and not showing it as red once you have one or more trackers as you mention that the goal is not and will never be to identify any trackers as bad or good. But showing it as red when you have some traces of a tracker seems a bad idea. If you do not want to identify trackers as good or bad (I get why you do not want to do that), maybe you should point to the number of trackers as good or bad by allowing more colors. Now you are already showing red when anyone has traces of 1, which seems to me as the bad message. If you want to promote having fewer trackers in apps, it should show it as an improvement if trackers are removed.

BTW I like what you are building here. It's just a matter of putting things in perspective.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: I think the point is being missed: all trackers are 3rd parties regardless of "good" or "bad", and whether or not they exist in an app is all that matters here. Exodus informs the user about these things, and its up to the (lay) user to contextualise that info however they see fit.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
> I think the point is being missed: all trackers are 3rd parties regardless of "good" or "bad", and whether or not they exist in an app is all that matters here. Exodus informs the user about these things, and its up to the (lay) user to contextualise that info however they see fit.

I understand the confusion.
However, not all trackers are 3rd parties. There are examples where the software used for tracking is running in the same private cloud as the app and the data is owned by the app itself. So a 3rd party would not have any access to this content, neither has visibility on anything that can identify a person like for example an IP address.
So currently these so-called "trackers" fall in the same boat as "trackers" where information is shared with the big tech companies.

In that sense, if an app opens a connection and stores any content in a database online (even if the database is owned by the developer), that connection by itself would be a tracker. Because the result would be exactly the same as using self-hosted analytics software.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body:
but you are talking about one use-case, your own. with an app and tracker using the same cloud storage etc.
what about all these apps:
https://reports.exodus-privacy.eu.org/en/trackers/122/

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
> May I suggest changing the color and not showing it as red once you have one or more trackers

> Now you are already showing red when anyone has traces of 1

That's not exactly the case. The badge is showing red only if there are 5 trackers or more, not just 1. If you have between 1 and 4 trackers, it will show yellow. Note that this indeed an arbitrary scale.

> There are examples where the software used for tracking is running in the same private cloud as the app and the data is owned by the app itself. So a 3rd party would not have any access to this content, neither has visibility on anything that can identify a person like for example an IP address.

Unfortunately it is more complex than that. Take Matomo (previously named Piwik): https://reports.exodus-privacy.eu.org/en/trackers/138/. This solution can be self-hosted or hosted on a 3rd party premises. How could we differentiate these 2 cases?
This is simply some work we cannot do for all the trackers in our database, not mentioning that it would most probably go against our neutrality principle.

comments.author: Participant 1
Participant 3
comments.body:
@Bramzor As you can read on our website:

> εxodus analyzes Android applications in order to list the embedded trackers. A tracker is a piece of software meant to collect data about you or your usages. So, εxodus reports tell you what are the ingredients of the cake.

Our goal is therefore not to score apps but to give make the information accessible to everyone. If a person or an organization wants to use our data to score apps based on privacy respect, our data is available and we even have a REST API which can be used for that purpose. Some organizations such as [/e/](https://e.foundation/products/) are already doing something similar.

Note that removing trackers (going from 4 trackers to 2) will still have impact on your reports though. You can then publicly explain from your side why you are using the remaining trackers. I think it is a good practice for transparency anyway.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Publicly explain the result would only be good if it could be added to εxodus too. Else I don't think it's a good idea to point towards tracker information you may not agree with.

Noticed that Facebook and Google apps are shown like they do not have any trackers in them. While we all know these apps are basically big trackers on their own.
